## Why This Is Asked
This question probes ability to reason about privacy-preserving telemetry at the device level, balancing DP budgets, user consent, and real-world rollout costs.

## Key Concepts
- Local differential privacy budgets (epsilon, delta)
- On-device data minimization and batching
- Energy and memory constraints on mobile devices
- Regulatory/compliance considerations and consent flows
- Rollout strategy and break-even analysis

## Code Example
```javascript
// Pseudo: batch events, apply DP, flush when online
let queue = [];
function addEvent(e){ queue.push(e); if(queue.length>=BATCH_SIZE) flush(); }
function flush(){ const noisy = applyDP(queue); send(noisy); queue=[]; }
```

## Follow-up Questions
- How would you estimate the DP budget for a user with 1k events/day?
- How would intermittent connectivity affect retention and accuracy of analytics?

## Why This Is Asked
Tests the ability to manage risk in live ML-style deployments, ensuring data integrity and latency goals while using feature flags and controlled rollouts.

## Key Concepts
- Canary deployments and feature flags
- Drift detection and rollback strategies
- Observability, alerts, and guardrails
- Auditability and versioning of models/artifacts

## Code Example
```javascript
// Pseudo drift check sketch
function driftOk(liveDist, offlineDist, thresh){
  const kl = klDiv(liveDist, offlineDist);
  return kl < thresh;
}
```

## Follow-up Questions
- How would you choose drift thresholds? Why different for users vs. admins?
- How would you structure pre-release validation and rollback testing before full reintroduction?
